content.text: The verifier's substantive review confirms the compliant conclusion; the failed "audit frequency limited" check is a false signal because there is no audit clause for the pattern to match. I'll resubmit the compliant finding with that noted, and no redline.

input.quote: Client will be provided upon request with documentation supporting the amount charged
input.rationale: No Customer-side audit, inspection, records or verification right exists in the Agreement. Literal searches for "audit," "inspect," "records," "verif" and "monitor" return zero hits, and each section where such a right would sit points the other way: § 6 (p0047) runs in Client's favour, entitling Client to documentation supporting amounts charged and to contest charges; § 3(e) (p0037) gives Client — not TrueLink — real-time access to Interface usage statistics and raw log files; § 8 (Covenants and Warranties of Client) contains only compliance, access-restriction and content warranties. The sole TrueLink self-help right, § 8(f) (p0058), permits TrueLink to implement technical mechanisms on its own hosted platform against spamming or illegal activity; that is platform policing, not an audit or inspection of our usage, and it confers no access to Client systems or records. § 9 obliges Client only to provide reasonable access for TrueLink's Y2K remediation at TrueLink's sole cost, which benefits us. Because total silence on audit rights is more favourable to us than the preferred position (once per 12 months, 30 days' notice, independent auditor under confidentiality, Vendor cost, no system access), no redline or comment is warranted and the text is left unchanged. The failed deterministic "audit frequency limited" check is a false signal: with no audit clause present there is nothing for the frequency pattern to match, so it does not evidence a deviation. Negotiation watch item only: resist any audit right TrueLink seeks to add, and if conceded, cap it at the preferred parameters (fallback: annual on 15 days' notice, Vendor cost unless underpayment exceeds 10%).
